questions.stem:
A small stone is projected vertically upwards from a point $O$ with a speed of $19.6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Modelling the stone as a particle moving freely under gravity,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the greatest height above $O$ reached by the stone,
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: complete method (which could involve use of two suvat equations) for finding $H$ i.e. for an equation in $H$ only, condone sign errors. A1: 19.6 or 20 correctly obtained (2g is A0)
$0^2 = 19.6^2 - 2gH$
$H=19.6\text{m}\,(20)$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) find the length of time for which the stone is more than $14.7\,\mathrm{m}$ above $O$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: for a quadratic equation in $t$ only (where $t$ is time at 14.7 above $O$). A1: for a correct equation. DM1: dependent on first M1, for solving for $t$. A1: for both values of $t$, 1 and 3. A1: for 2 s. N.B. If answer(s) are wrong or have come from an incorrect quadratic, and the quadratic formula has been used, M1 can only be awarded if there is clear evidence that the correct formula has been used. If their expression is not correct for their quadratic, allow a slip but only if we see an attempt to substitute into a stated correct formula. N.B. Obtaining $t=1$ at $s=14.7$ (above $O$) only, can score max M1 A1.
$14.7 = 19.6t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$
$t^2-4t+3=0$
$(t-1)(t-3)=0$
$t=1$ or $3$; Answer 2 s
ALT 1: (their $h-14.7$)$=\frac{1}{2}gt^2$ OR $v^2=19.6^2-2g\times14.7 \Rightarrow v=(\pm)9.8$ and $0\ 9.8-9.8t \Rightarrow t=1$ (M1 A1); Total $=2\times$ their 1 $=2$ s (DM1 A1).
ALT 2/3: $v^2=19.6^2-2g\times14.7$, $v=\pm9.8$ (M1 A1); EITHER: $-9.8=9.8-gT$, $T=2$ (DM1 A1); OR: $0=9.8t-\frac{1}{2}gt^2$, $t=(0)$ or 2 (DM1 A1).

questions.stem:
A particle of mass 2 kg is suspended from a horizontal ceiling by two light inextensible strings, $PR$ and $QR$. The particle hangs at $R$ in equilibrium, with the strings in a vertical plane. The string $PR$ is inclined at $55°$ to the horizontal and the string $QR$ is inclined at $35°$ to the horizontal, as shown in Figure 1.

Find

parts.text:
(i) the tension in the string $PR$,
(ii) the tension in the string $QR$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: resolving horizontally with correct no. of terms and both $T_P$ and $T_Q$ terms resolved (M0 if they assume $T_P=T_Q$). A1: for a correct equation $T_P\cos55=T_Q\cos35$. M1: resolving vertically with correct no. of terms and both $T_P$ and $T_Q$ terms resolved (M0 if they assume $T_P=T_Q$). A1: for a correct equation $T_P\sin55+T_Q\sin35=2g$. M1: (independent) for eliminating either $T_P$ or $T_Q$. A1: for $T_P=16$ N or 16.1 N. A1: for $T_Q=11$ N or 11.2 N. N.B. If both are given to more than 3SF, deduct the third A1.
ALT 1 (resolving along each string): M2 for resolving along one of the strings, e.g. $T_P=2g\cos35°$; A1 for a correct equation ($T_P=2g\sin35°$ scores M2A0A0); A1 for $T_P=16$(N) or 16.1(N); M1 for resolving along the other string, e.g. $T_Q=2g\cos55°$; A1 for a correct equation ($T_Q=2g\sin55°$ scores M1A0A0); A1 for $T_Q=11$(N) or 11.2(N).
ALT 2 (using a Triangle of Forces): Both equations in Alt 1 could come from using sohcahtoa or the Sine Rule on a triangle of forces, marked the same way. Once either $T_P$ or $T_Q$ is found, they could use $T_P=T_Q\tan55°$ or $T_Q=T_P\tan55°$ (equivalent to horizontal resolution) or Pythagoras. e.g. $T_P=2g\cos35°$ (M2, First A1) $=16$(N) or 16.1(N) (Third A1); $T_Q=T_P\tan35°$ or $\sqrt{(2g)^2-(T_P)^2}$ (M1, Second A1) $=11$(N) or 11.2(N) (Fourth A1).
N.B. If they are clearly using the Sine Rule but have say 35°, 55° and 80° in their triangle, all 3 M marks would be available and at most 1 A mark, e.g. $T_P=\frac{2g\sin55}{\sin80}$ (M2 A0A0), $T_Q=\frac{T_P\sin35}{\sin55}$ (M1 Second A1 A0).

questions.stem: A lift of mass 200 kg is being lowered into a mineshaft by a vertical cable attached to the top of the lift. A crate of mass 55 kg is on the floor inside the lift, as shown in Figure 2. The lift descends vertically with constant acceleration. There is a constant upwards resistance of magnitude 150 N on the lift. The crate experiences a constant normal reaction of magnitude 473 N from the floor of the lift.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the acceleration of the lift.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: for an equation in $a$ only, with usual rules. A1: for a correct equation. A1: for $1.2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Allow $-1.2\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ if appropriate.
For crate, $55g-473=55a$
$a=1.2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the magnitude of the force exerted on the lift by the cable.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: for an equation, in $T$ and $a$, for the system or the lift only, with usual rules ($a$ does not need to be a numerical value). A2 (-1 each error): for a correct equation (Allow $\pm T$). We do not need to see a numerical value for $a$. A1: for 2040 (N) or 2000 (N). N.B. In both parts of this question use the mass which is being used to guide you as to which part of the system is being considered.
For system: $55g+200g\pm T-150=255a$, Magnitude $=2040$ N or 2000 N
OR
For lift: $200g+473-150\pm T=200a$, Magnitude $=2040$ N or 2000 N

questions.stem: A beam $AB$ has length 5 m and mass 25 kg. The beam is suspended in equilibrium in a horizontal position by two vertical ropes. One rope is attached to the beam at $A$ and the other rope is attached to the point $C$ on the beam where $CB = 0.5$ m, as shown in Figure 3. A particle $P$ of mass 60 kg is attached to the beam at $B$ and the beam remains in equilibrium in a horizontal position. The beam is modelled as a uniform rod and the ropes are modelled as light strings.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find
(i) the tension in the rope attached to the beam at $A$,
(ii) the tension in the rope attached to the beam at $C$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) First M1 for a moments or vertical resolution equation, with correct no. of terms and dimensionally correct. First A1 for a correct equation. Second M1 for a moments equation, with correct no. of terms and dimensionally correct. Second A1 for a correct equation. Third A1 for 44 (N) or 43.6 (N) or $\frac{40g}{9}$. Fourth A1 for 790 (N) or 789 (N) or $\frac{725g}{9}$. Deduct 1 mark for inexact multiples of $g$. N.B. If they assume that both tensions are the same, can only score max M1 in (a) for M(A) or M(C). If a vertical resolution is used, give marks for this equation FIRST. If not, enter marks for each moments equation in the order in which they appear.
$T_A+T_C=85g$ OR $M(A)$: $25g\times2.5+60g\times5=4.5\times T_C$ OR $M(C)$: $T_A\times4.5+60g\times0.5=25g\times2$ OR $M(B)$: $T_A\times5+T_C\times0.5=25g\times2.5$ OR $M(G)$: $T_A\times2.5+60g\times2.5=2\times T_C$
$T_A=\frac{40g}{9}=44$N or 43.6N; $T_C=\frac{725g}{9}=790$N or 789 N

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Particle $P$ is removed and replaced by a particle $Q$ of mass $M$ kg at $B$. Given that the beam remains in equilibrium in a horizontal position,
(b) find
(i) the greatest possible value of $M$,
(ii) the greatest possible tension in the rope attached to the beam at $C$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
SCHEME CHANGE: B1 BECOMES THE FOURTH A1. First M1 for a moments equation with $T_A=0$. First A1 for a correct equation. Second A1 for $M=100$. Second M1 for a(nother) moments or vertical resolution equation with $T_A=0$. Third A1 for a correct equation. Fourth A1 (B1) for $T_C=125g$ or 1230 (N) or 1200 (N). N.B. Some candidates may need to solve 2 simultaneous equations in $M$ and $T_C$ and so will earn the 'equation' marks before they earn Second and Fourth A(B) marks. If a vertical resolution is used, give marks for this equation SECOND. If not, enter marks for each moments equation in the order in which they appear.
The possible equations are: $T_C=25g+Mg$; $M(C)$: $25g\times2=Mg\times0.5$; $M(A)$: $25g\times2.5+5Mg=4.5T_C$; $M(B)$: $25g\times2.5=T_C\times0.5$; $M(G)$: $T_C\times2=Mg\times2.5$. Any two of these can each earn M1A1 (M0 if incorrect no. of terms). Then Second A1 for $M=100$. And Fourth A1 (B1) for $T_C=125g$ or 1230 or 1200.
N.B. No marks in (b) if they use any answers from (a) or $M=60$.
$M(C)$, $25g\times2=Mg\times0.5$
$M=100$
$T_C=25g+100g$
$T_C=125g$ (1200 or 1230)N

questions.stem:
A particle $P$ is moving with constant velocity. The position vector of $P$ at time $t$ seconds ($t \geqslant 0$) is $\mathbf{r}$ metres, relative to a fixed origin $O$, and is given by
$\mathbf{r} = (2t-3)\mathbf{i} + (4-5t)\mathbf{j}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the initial position vector of $P$.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1 for $(-3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$ (m). Allow column vectors throughout.
$\mathbf{r} = (-3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$ m

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The particle $P$ passes through the point with position vector $(3.4\mathbf{i} - 12\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m}$ at time $T$ seconds.

(b) Find the value of $T$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1 for a clear attempt at either $3.4(\mathbf{i})=(2T-3)(\mathbf{i})$ or $-12(\mathbf{j})=(4-5T)(\mathbf{j})$. First A1 for a correct equation (either) without $\mathbf{i}$'s and $\mathbf{j}$'s. A1 for 3.2 oe. N.B. $T=\frac{6.4\mathbf{i}-16\mathbf{j}}{2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}}=3.2$ scores M1A1A1 BUT if RHS is not a single number, then M0. Also, if they get 3.2 and another value and don't clearly choose 3.2 then A0.
$3.4=2T-3$ or $-12=4-5T$
$T=3.2$

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) First M1 for a complete method for finding $\mathbf{v}$, e.g. $\mathbf{r}=(-3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})+t(2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})$ so $\mathbf{v}=2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}$ OR $\mathbf{v}=\frac{(3.4\mathbf{i}-12\mathbf{j})-(-3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})}{\text{their }T}$ OR $\mathbf{v}=\frac{d\mathbf{r}}{dt}=2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}$. First A1 for $2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}$; M1A1 can be awarded for $2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}$ only. Second M1 for attempt to find magnitude of their $\mathbf{v}$, i.e. $\sqrt{2^2+(-5)^2}$. Second A1 for $\sqrt{29}$ or 5.4 or better.
OR: First M1 for attempt to find distance travelled: $d=\sqrt{(-3-3.4)^2+(4--12)^2}$; First A1 if correct; Second M1 for their $d$/their $T$; Second A1 for $\sqrt{29}$ or 5.4 or better.
$\mathbf{r} = (-3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})+t(2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})$
$\mathbf{v} = 2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}$
speed $=\sqrt{(2^2+(-5)^2)}=\sqrt{29}=5.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ or better
Alt (c): $|\mathbf{s}|=\sqrt{6.4^2+(-16)^2}=17.23...$ (M1 A1); speed $=\frac{17.23}{3.2}=5.4$ or better (M1 A1)

questions.stem: A train travels along a straight horizontal track between two stations, $A$ and $B$. The train starts from rest at $A$ and moves with constant acceleration $0.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ until it reaches a speed of $V\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, ($V < 50$). The train then travels at this constant speed before it moves with constant deceleration $0.25\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ until it comes to rest at $B$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Sketch in the space below a speed-time graph for the motion of the train between the two stations $A$ and $B$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) B1 for a trapezium with line starting and finishing on the $t$-axis (shape). B1 for $V$ correctly marked.

parts.label: b
parts.text:

Two particles $P$ and $Q$ have mass 4 kg and 0.5 kg respectively. The particles are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string. Particle $P$ is held at rest on a fixed rough plane, which is inclined to the horizontal at an angle $\alpha$ where $\tan\alpha = \frac{4}{3}$. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is 0.5. The string lies along the plane and passes over a small smooth light pulley which is fixed at the top of the plane. Particle $Q$ hangs freely at rest vertically below the pulley. The string lies in the vertical plane which contains the pulley and a line of greatest slope of the inclined plane, as shown in Figure 4. Particle $P$ is released from rest with the string taut and slides down the plane.

Given that $Q$ has not hit the pulley, find

(11)
